title: 2020 AMC 10B Problem 12
statement: The decimal representation of \[\frac{1}{20^{20}}\] consists of a string of zeros after the decimal point, followed by a \(9\) and then several more digits. How many zeros are in that initial string of zeros after the decimal point?

solutions.text:
We can write \[\frac{1}{20^{20}}=\frac{1}{(4\cdot5)^{20}}=\frac{5^{20}}{10^{40}}.\] Now \(5^{20}=95{,}367{,}431{,}640{,}625,\) which has \(14\) digits and begins with \(9.\) Dividing by \(10^{40}\) places this \(14\)-digit number after the decimal point with \(40-14=26\) zeros before the first digit.

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: Find how many digits \(5^{20}\) has to know how many leading zeros appear
